subject.title: Add an FxTwitter read transport for public lookups, threads, profiles, and search

question: Should Birdclaw adopt FxTwitter as a core, explicitly selected public-read transport with optional self-hosted endpoint support?
rationale: The architecture can accommodate another attributable source, but choosing to support this third-party service establishes product commitments around privacy, reliability, configuration safety, capability guarantees, and ongoing API compatibility that cannot be inferred from existing behavior.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow MVP
options.body: Approve explicit post, thread, conversation, profile, public-status, and search reads while prohibiting automatic fallback and authenticated-account operations.

options.title: Defer pending transport direction
options.body: Keep the proposal open until the supported bird and xurl transport strategy and shared capability model are settled.

options.title: Decline core integration
options.body: Limit core live reads to approved authenticated transports and leave FxTwitter experimentation outside Birdclaw's supported source contract.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a narrow MVP
recommendation.body: Approve explicit post, thread, conversation, profile, public-status, and search reads while prohibiting automatic fallback and authenticated-account operations.

likelyOwner.reason: The repository vision names Peter Steinberger as product owner, and this choice changes the supported live-source contract.
